title: FleetIO: Managing Multi-Tenant Cloud Storage with Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
problem: Cloud virtualized flash storage (SSD) systems must simultaneously support software-isolated and hardware-isolated tenant instances, but face a fundamental tension between performance isolation (preventing noisy neighbors) and resource utilization efficiency — strong isolation wastes storage, while weak isolation causes long-tail latency.
motivation: Multi-tenant cloud SSD platforms have long struggled to jointly achieve performance isolation and high resource utilization, a problem that worsens as workload diversity increases and SSDs become the primary storage substrate.
method: FleetIO applies multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) to dynamically manage storage resources across multiple tenants. Each tenant is managed by a separate RL agent that learns policies for I/O scheduling, resource allocation, and admission control. The agents coordinate through shared environment observations to balance per-tenant performance isolation with global storage utilization. The MARL framework enables adaptive responses to changing workload patterns without requiring hand-tuned policies, jointly optimizing tail latency and utilization.
key_novelty: Applying multi-agent reinforcement learning to cloud SSD resource management, where per-tenant agents jointly learn to balance isolation and utilization through shared environment feedback.
contributions: FleetIO: a multi-agent RL system for managing multi-tenant cloud flash storage
Joint optimization of performance isolation and resource utilization via MARL
Support for both software-isolated and hardware-isolated storage instance types
Demonstration of adaptive storage management under varying multi-tenant workloads

limitations: MARL training overhead, convergence time, and generalization to unseen workloads not discussed in abstract.
